Rulebooks as spreadsheets

Source: R/xlsx.R
rulebook_template.Rd

For people who would rather not write YAML or R, a rulebook can be kept as an Excel workbook. rulebook_template() writes an annotated, empty workbook (or one filled from an existing rulebook) with drop-down lists for every choice; read_rulebook() reads it back.

Usage

rulebook_template(path, rb = NULL)

Arguments

path

Path of the .xlsx file to write.

rb

Optional rulebook to fill the template from.

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

The workbook has one sheet per kind of rule:

SheetOne row per
plansetting (plan details, defaults, conversion, ground budget, morphology)
zoneszone: height, site ratios, building form, density, uses
setbacksyard, plane or other setback, with its conditions
bandsband of a value that changes in steps (e.g. coverage by site area)
familieszone family
overlaysoverlay
areasprecinct or other area
changesset of zone changes made by an overlay, area or sub-area
bonuses, entitlementsbonus or entitlement
unmodelledrule not modelled
variants, unit_mix, access_widththe rarer tables
fields(read-only) what every column means

In setbacks, bands and access_width, the target column names what the row belongs to: a zone key (MRZ), an overlay's changes (overlay:character), an area's changes (area:quarry), an area's changes for one zone (area:quarry/zone:MRZ) or a sub-area (area:quarry/sub:B).

Lists inside a cell are comma-separated (side, rear). Any number may be a formula, written as text (max(3, 0.4 * H)).

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
rulebook_template(f)
openxlsx2::wb_load(f)$sheet_names
#>  [1] "README"       "plan"         "zones"        "setbacks"     "bands"       
#>  [6] "families"     "overlays"     "areas"        "changes"      "bonuses"     
#> [11] "entitlements" "unmodelled"   "variants"     "unit_mix"     "access_width"
#> [16] "fields"
